title: Brucie Smashes: No Banner only HULK Opens 2026 With 177.86 and a Message
dek: Ramon flattened the Dawgs by nearly 80 points, Randy's Bears-flavored lineup bullied JMoney, Zoe won her first fantasy game ever, and Sonny squeaked past Philly in the first eight-team Sunday in league history.
body: The Buckaroo Football League went to eight teams this year, and Ramon apparently took that as a challenge to be eight times louder. No Banner only HULK hung 177.86 points on Mekhi's Dawgs, a 79.5-point beatdown in a game the Dawgs were actually favored to win at 54%. Josh Allen threw in 35.66, Kenneth Walker III ran for 32.6, and D'Andre Swift added 31.9 on a projection of 11.41. The title-odds model watched all of it and jumped Brucie from 11% to 47%, which is the analytics equivalent of standing up and spilling its drink. A Chicago kid who now roots for Buffalo rode a Bills quarterback to the top of the league in week 1; the Bears fans in this group will be thrilled.

If there's a footnote to the HULK masterpiece, it's that it came with a defense that scored -4. The Texans D/ST, projected for 5.25, actively subtracted from the total, and Ramon still won by almost 80. That's either a terrifying sign for the rest of the league or proof that the scoring gods spent all their luck on one roster. Either way, nobody in this league got a lead like that on Sunday, and nobody is going to want to see that lineup in a few weeks.

Randy wasn't far behind in the bully rankings. The fumblers dropped 146.16 on Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV, which managed just 75.96, the week's lowest score by more than 20 points. Caleb Williams went for 37.26, the best performance of the week, on a 16.39 projection, and Derrick Henry chipped in 34.8. Randy's Bears loyalty does have a cost, though: rookie tight end Colston Loveland posted a clean 0 against a 9.67 projection. When you outscore your opponent by 70, you can afford a tight end who took the day off emotionally.

JMoney's afternoon got worse the longer you stared at it. Ashton Jeanty sat on his bench and scored 29.7, the kind of number that would have turned a blowout into merely a loss. Counting or not Counting GV now sits eighth with 3% playoff odds and 0% title odds, a projection that feels harsh after one week but is not going to lose sleep over it. The good news is that week 2 brings a 1-0 team that only scored 106.42, so a rebound is very much on the table.

The week's best story might be the quietest one. Zoe, playing the first fantasy game of her life, took Ghostu-Spider SZN to a 129.56 to 108.6 win over Kaushal, a two-time Buckaroo Bowl champion, as a 48% underdog at home. Z² did leave David Montgomery's 27.4 points on the bench, so the rookie still has some lineup homework, but she won by 21 anyway. Habib, meanwhile, watched his title odds crater from 17% to 3% after one loss, and the only move on his ledger was swapping Browns D/ST for Jaguars D/ST. That's a lot of faith in a defense to fix a 21-point gap.

Over at the closest game of the week, Sonny's The Horse is Hea edged Team Pillbert 106.42 to 102.1, winning as a 46% underdog. Jahmyr Gibbs gave Philly 31.1 points and it still wasn't enough, which is a tough way to open a season. Sonny was also the week's busiest manager on the wire, picking up Mark Andrews and cutting T.J. Hockenson, a tight end swap that will be judged entirely on whether Andrews shows up in week 2. Despite the win, the model dropped The Horse is Hea from 9% to 4% title odds; apparently squeaking by isn't the kind of win it respects.

Then there's Kai, who had the roughest Sunday in the league, and not just because of the scoreboard. Ja'Marr Chase posted 2.2 points on a 16.44 projection, Brock Bowers didn't play at all and sat in the starting lineup anyway, and Christian Watson scored 29.7 from the bench. Starting an inactive Bowers is on the manager, not the player, and for the guy who drafted from overseas this year, it was the kind of lineup slip that stings. The Dawgs' title odds fell from 17% to 1%, the steepest drop in the league.

Week 2 delivers the headliner right away: No Banner only HULK hosts the rookie in Ramon vs. Zoe, a battle of 1-0 teams with a combined 307 points. Randy and the fumblers face a Dawgs team desperate to avoid 0-2, Philly and Habib meet in a showdown of week-1 losers who both entered with real title hopes, and JMoney gets a crack at Sonny. One week in, the top four are all undefeated, the bottom four are all winless, and the gap between them is exactly one game. Plenty of time to panic properly.

social.text: Week 1 final: No Banner only HULK 177.86, Dawgs 98.36. The fumblers 146.16, Counting or not Counting GV 75.96. Ghostu-Spider SZN 129.56, Habibsters 108.6. The Horse is Hea 106.42, Team Pillbert 102.1. Four teams sit at 1-0 to open the eight-team era.

social.author: No Banner only HULK
social.text: 177.86. Matchday one, done. Player of the week shoutout to Josh Allen (35.66), with Kenneth Walker III and D'Andre Swift both over 30. On to week 2. 💚

social.author: Marcus Pell
social.text: Hot take after one week: the 47% title odds for No Banner only HULK are too LOW. They scored 177.86 with a defense that went -4. Fix the D/ST and this is a wrecking ball.

social.author: Gridiron Gary
social.text: Zoe beat a two-time champ in her FIRST EVER fantasy game while benching 27.4 points. The rookie is not here to learn, she's here to collect.

social.author: Windy City Waiver Hawk
social.text: Caleb Williams 37.26 on Randy's team. Somewhere Randy is refusing to trade him already and nobody has even asked.

social.author: Bench Points Betty
social.text: Ashton Jeanty: 29.7 on the bench. Christian Watson: 29.7 on the bench. David Montgomery: 27.4 on the bench. Week 1 bench all-stars would've won two matchups on its own.

social.author: Ghostu-Spider SZN Fan Club
social.text: 1-0. Beat the Habibsters. Next up: the 177-point monster. We fear nothing. 🕷️🧀

social.author: Start Sit Stan
social.text: PSA to every manager: check the inactives before kickoff. Brock Bowers did not play, and he was still in a starting lineup. Ouch, Dawgs.

bios.1: Sonny's defending champ edged Team Pillbert 106.42 to 102.1 as a slight underdog, then swapped T.J. Hockenson for Mark Andrews on the wire. The model wasn't impressed, trimming title odds to 4%, but a 1-0 start is a 1-0 start. A week-2 date with Jordan is a chance to pile on.
bios.2: Randy's crew bullied Counting or not Counting GV 146.16 to 75.96 behind Caleb Williams' week-best 37.26 and 34.8 from Derrick Henry. Title odds nearly doubled to 28%, even with Colston Loveland posting a zero. Next up: a Dawgs team with something to prove.
bios.3: Jordan's team managed 75.96, the week's lowest score, in a 70-point loss to The fumblers while Ashton Jeanty's 29.7 sat on the bench. The model has JMoney at 3% playoff odds after one week. A week-2 shot at Sonny is the best way to make it look silly.
bios.4: Alan got 31.1 from Jahmyr Gibbs and still came up 4.32 points short of The Horse is Hea in the week's closest game. Title odds slid from 14% to 4%. Philly gets Habib in week 2, a matchup of two teams that expected to be 1-0.
bios.5: Mekhi's week was a pileup: 98.36 points, a 79.5-point loss, Ja'Marr Chase at 2.2, Brock Bowers starting and not playing, and 29.7 from Christian Watson stranded on the bench. Title odds crashed from 17% to 1%, the biggest fall in the league. Kai faces The fumblers next and needs a cleaner lineup to stop the slide.
bios.6: Kaushal's two-time champs lost 129.56 to 108.6 to a first-year manager and watched their title odds tumble from 17% to 3%. The fix so far is a defense swap, Browns out, Jaguars in. A week-2 meeting with Team Pillbert is a must-have to avoid an 0-2 hole.
bios.7: Ramon opened 2026 with a 177.86-point demolition of the Dawgs, the biggest score of the week by more than 30 points. Josh Allen, Kenneth Walker III and D'Andre Swift all topped 30, and the title odds leapt from 11% to 47%. Now the only question is who slows them down, starting with Zoe in week 2.
bios.8: Zoe's first fantasy game ever ended in a 129.56 to 108.6 win over the two-time champion Habibsters. She left 27.4 points from David Montgomery on the bench and won by 21 anyway. Week 2 brings the league's hottest team, a real test for the 1-0 rookie.
